Introduction
The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) is committed to solving complex problems with innovative ideas and producing high impact research that benefits both industry and society. Major research endeavours within the Department on the following areas:
- Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Materials Engineering
- Communications and Information Security
- Electric Vehicles and Smart Mobility
- Microelectronics and Quantum Technology
- Photonics and Smart Devices
- Power and Energy Systems
Currently, over hundreds of research projects are being undertaken. These projects are mostly funded by the Hong Kong government, the Chinese mainland central and provincial governments, and our industrial partners. Many of our research degree graduates continue their career paths by becoming a researcher/an academic in local/mainland/overseas institutions, or joining international renowned companies.
Our students’ research is supported by enthusiastic faculty members and support staff, who ensure that the Department provides students with a positive and nurturing academic environment.
The Department ensures that all research students have opportunities to enrich their research experience through research exchange visits, attendance at leading international conferences, and participation in global competitions and departmental projects.
Applications are now invited for registration in our programme leading to the Degree of Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)/Master of Philosophy (MPhil) by research in EEE. Please browse the e-prospectus to learn more about our research degree programmes and EEE research interests.
We look forward to welcoming you to EEE!

Supporting Documents
Academic Referee's Report
Compulsory - Two Academic Referee's Reports are required. To apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS), academic referees must complete online referee's reports before the HKPFS application deadline.
• Identify and invite two academics who are familiar with your academic performance and achievements. Proposed supervisor(s) from the PolyU, proposed supervisor(s) from the partner institution (if any), and persons from non-academic backgrounds are not considered appropriate academic referees.
• Provide complete and accurate information on your referees, including their email addresses under a university or an organisation, in your online application.
